question:
(a) Describe the motion of free electrons in a conductor before and after applying an electric field.
(b) Explain why drift velocity is small although current is established almost instantly.

options.A:
(a) Before applying an electric field, free electrons move randomly and their average velocity is zero. After applying it, they experience force $-e\vec E$ and acquire a small drift velocity opposite to $\vec E$.
(b) Frequent collisions with lattice ions keep drift velocity small, but the electric field is established throughout the conductor almost instantly, so current begins quickly.
options.B:
(a) Electrons are stationary before an electric field and move in the direction of the field after it is applied.
(b) Drift velocity is large because electrons travel at the speed of light.
options.C:
(a) Random thermal motion itself causes a net current before the field is applied.
(b) The current takes a long time to begin because the field moves slowly.
options.D:
(a) Electrons move only in one direction before the field is applied.
(b) Drift velocity is small because the electric field is absent.
